props.headline: One Data Foundation for Enterprise Apps and AI Agents
props.subheadline: Enterprises and AI-native teams start from different places. They end up needing the same database: one that scales without giving up consistency. TiDB is built for both.

items.description: By three infrastructure engineers, as an open source project

items.label: Data in a single cluster
items.description: Up from 1 PB a year earlier, alongside 3M+ tables per cluster

items.description: Up from tens of thousands six months earlier

items.label: Created by AI agents

props.title: Different Starting Points, One Data Foundation
props.subtitle: Our mission is to give engineers a database that keeps up, whether the user is a person or an agent. Our theme for 2026 is infinite agents and infinite data, running on the same infrastructure. Enterprise systems and AI agents are converging on the same requirements from opposite directions, and TiDB serves both.

items.title: Enterprise: Infinite Data
items.description: Consolidate database fleets, migrate with zero downtime, and run across regions with the consistency core systems depend on.

items.title: AI-Native: Infinite Agents
items.description: Give every agent its own isolated database in under a second, with vectors, transactions, and analytics in one engine and state that outlives the session.

props.title: Proven by Enterprises and AI Pioneers

items.title: 750+ PostgreSQL Clusters Consolidated into 16
items.description: Atlassian serves tens of millions of active users across Jira and Confluence, and runs its Forge SQL service on TiDB with more than 3 million tables.

items.title: A Graph Service Modernized on Distributed SQL
items.description: Pinterest moved its graph service to TiDB and cut infrastructure cost by around half.

items.title: From Viral Launch to 1.5M+ Clusters
items.description: Manus migrated to TiDB Cloud in two weeks and has since scaled to more than 1.5 million clusters behind its agents.

items.title: 1M+ Persistent Filesystems for Agents
items.description: Moonshot AI's Kimi runs more than one million persistent filesystems on TiDB Cloud Filesystem and cut data infrastructure costs by an order of magnitude.

props.title: Built in the Open Since 2015
props.subtitle: PingCAP was founded by three infrastructure engineers who wanted a better way to run databases at scale. They built it as open source, and that is still how TiDB is made.

items.title: Founded as Open Source
items.description: TiDB starts as an open source project and stays that way. Hundreds of contributors join over the years, and its storage layer, TiKV, becomes a CNCF Graduated project.

items.title: TiDB X Announced
items.description: A new architecture that puts object storage at the backbone of TiDB, unveiled at the 2025 keynote.

items.label: October 2026
items.title: TiDB SCaiLE 2026
items.description: TiDB X now powers every new TiDB Cloud cluster by default. New: TiDB Cloud Zero for agents, TiDB Cloud Premium GA planned for November, plus BYOC, TiDB Cloud Filesystem, and PostgreSQL support on Starter in public preview.

items.label: End of 2026
items.title: TiDB X Core Goes Open Source
items.description: The core code of TiDB X is planned to be open sourced by the end of 2026, with a zero-downtime rolling upgrade path from TiDB classic targeted for October 2027.

items.a: TiDB is the distributed SQL database for enterprise applications and AI agents. It runs transactions, analytics, and vector search in one engine, with MySQL compatibility and PostgreSQL support in public preview on TiDB Cloud Starter.

TiDB X is TiDB's new architecture. It separates compute from storage, and separates heavy background work like indexing and compaction from online transactions, so latency stays flat as workloads grow. It powers every new TiDB Cloud cluster by default.
PingCAP was founded in 2015 by three infrastructure engineers. TiDB has been open source from the start.
TiDB is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, and serves customers worldwide.
Max Liu is the co-founder and CEO.
Yes. TiDB and its storage layer, TiKV, are open source, and TiKV is a CNCF Graduated project. The core code of TiDB X is planned to be open sourced by the end of 2026.
